newsitem.title: FRANCE: Analyst cautious on French wheat yield after rains.
newsitem.headline: Analyst cautious on French wheat yield after rains.

text.p: Heavy rain in late June and early July had a mixed impact on French crops, making it very difficult to predict yields for the 1997 soft wheat harvest, French analyst Strategie Grains said.

The rain helped grain development in northern and central France and in the southwest and the Poitou-Charente area. But it stopped the harvest in southern France and led to disease outbreaks in the north, the analyst said.
This mixed picture led Strategie Grains to maintain its estimates for French soft wheat and barley yields unchanged from the previous month.
It expects the national soft wheat yield to decline to 6.96 tonnes per hectare from 7.27 tonnes and the barley yield to drop to 5.89 tonnes from 6.19 last year.
"Without these persisting rains, we would have raised the French wheat yield to 7.05 tonnes per hectare from 6.96 tonnes last month", it said.

Strategie Grains expects France to harvest a 1997 soft wheat crop of 34.11 million tonnes against a record 34.69 million in 1996. It put the barley crop at 9.67 million tonnes against 9.46 million in 1996.
